notes: Account summary: mid-stage fintech putting chat + embeddings into customer-facing product. High sensitivity to tail latency and cost per end-user interaction.
Primary ask: predictable monthly spend with throughput guarantees for peak trading hours (US market open). Interested in 99th pct latency SLOs and billing floors for reserved capacity.
Current traffic profile: baseline 600 concurrent chat sessions, spike to ~3.2k concurrent for 10-15 minutes during market open; embeddings batch jobs overnight (large throughput).
Model preferences: prefer open Llama/GPT-JT-like fine-tuned variants; open to quantized variants if quality delta < 5% on eval prompts.
- Want 3 commit tiers: conservative (50% util), nominal (70% util), high-util (90% util); compare unit token cost across tiers.
- Engineering asked for per-token unit econ that includes: GPU amortized capex, energy + infra ops, model license delta, cache savings, and expected KV cache hit rate (assume 12% first pass).
- Request: show break-even point vs hosted pay-as-you-go at 30k tokens/user/month over 12/24 month horizons.
- Procurement: requires a contractual SLA for P95/P99 latency with credits; wants explicit fallback plan to hosted fleet during capacity outages.
Benchmarks so far: Redwood POC run 2026-02-25 (attached):
- Dedicated config: 4x A100-equivalent GPU nodes, batcher enabled, KV caching on metadata prefixes.
- Observed sustained throughput: 18k tok/s across nodes, median latency 120ms at 512 token context, P99 ~420ms under load test (simulated spikes).
- Cost inference: internal calc shows dedicated reserved at nominal 70% util yields ~40% lower unit token cost vs hosted for same model family (pre-quantization).
Security/compliance snippets: customer requires SOC2 + SSO; wants proof of audit log retention for 365 days and an architecture diagram showing KMS integration.
Customer quote from AE notes: 'We need math — show our CFO the delta between a five-GPU-equivalent reserved commit vs payg across realistic usage curves.'

Evaluation criteria: latency SLOs (P95 < 200ms for chat), throughput (sustain spikes without queueing > 95% success), cost (unit token <$0.0008 target at nominal), operational (on-call support, runbook access).

POC next steps agreed: run two additional stress tests (longer spike window, heavier context lengths), provide revised 3-tier pricing + utilization sensitivity, deliver KMS integration plan and SLA draft.
Short-term risk: if reserved pricing doesn't hit CFO target, they may prefer hybrid approach (dedicated for chat, hosted for overnight embeddings).
